title.rendered: Her Sins, Which Are Many, Are Forgiven: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Her sins, which are many, are forgiven — for she loved much.” A morning devotional on the woman with the alabaster jar.

content.rendered:
She walked uninvited into a Pharisee’s dinner party, alabaster jar in hand, and knelt at the feet of Jesus. Simon watched in disgust. Jesus received her tears without a word. What she did that evening became one of the most famous acts of worship in the New Testament.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, September 12, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Then He said to her, ‘Your sins are forgiven.’ And those who sat at the table with Him began to say to themselves, ‘Who is this who even forgives sins?’ Then He said to the woman, ‘Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.'”
Luke 7:48-50 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Simon the Pharisee was hosting a dinner party. Jesus was the guest. And in the middle of the meal, uninvited and unwelcome, a woman walked in. Luke does not name her. He simply calls her “a woman in the city who was a sinner.” In the language of first-century Judea, that phrase carried a specific and unmistakable meaning. She was known. Everyone in the room knew her, and knew what she had done. She was the last person any respectable dinner party in Israel would have wanted to see. And yet she came. She brought with her an alabaster flask of expensive fragrant oil. She knelt behind Jesus at the low table. And she began to weep. Her tears fell on His feet. She let down her hair, which no respectable woman would do in public, and wiped His feet with it. She kissed His feet. And she poured the oil over them.

Simon watched in silent disgust. Luke tells us his exact thoughts. “This Man, if He were a prophet, would know who and what manner of woman this is who is touching Him, for she is a sinner.” Jesus, who had heard Simon’s thoughts even though Simon had said nothing out loud, told Simon a short parable about two debtors, one who owed five hundred denarii and one who owed fifty, both forgiven. “Which of them will love him more?” Simon answered correctly. The one who was forgiven more. And Jesus turned the whole dinner on its head. “Do you see this woman? I entered your house; you gave Me no water for My feet, but she has washed My feet with her tears and wiped them with the hair of her head. You gave Me no kiss, but this woman has not ceased to kiss My feet. You did not anoint My head with oil, but this woman has anointed My feet with fragrant oil. Therefore I say to you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven, for she loved much. But to whom little is forgiven, the same loves little.”

Then Jesus said the words to her that she had come, without daring to hope, to hear. “Your sins are forgiven.” The Passion Translation renders it: “Then Jesus said to the woman at his feet, ‘All your sins are forgiven'” (Luke 7:48 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “And He said to her, Your sins are forgiven!” (Luke 7:48 AMPC). The exclamation is not decoration. It is the sound of a woman’s whole life turning around at a Pharisee’s dinner table.

The other guests began to murmur. “Who is this who even forgives sins?” But Jesus was not finished with the woman. He turned to her one more time and said, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.” Faith. Not her tears. Not her expensive oil. Not her willingness to break social convention. Her faith in Him. The forgiveness had been bought at the cross that Jesus was walking toward. The woman was receiving, in advance, what would be finished in a few short months on Calvary. And she left the dinner a different woman, forgiven, loved, and free.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this story is for anyone who has been carrying a past. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, if there is a Simon in your life whose eyes still see your history, if there is a version of yourself the world has not forgotten, if there is a weight of many sins you have been carrying, the invitation is to do what the woman at the dinner did. Come to Jesus. Bring the tears. Bring the alabaster jar of whatever is precious to you. Kneel at His feet. Faith reaches for the One who forgives. And His response is the same today as it was that evening in Simon’s house. Your sins are forgiven. Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that in Christ my sins, which are many, are forgiven. The price has been paid at the cross. I refuse to let the eyes of any Simon in my life keep me from Jesus. I bring my tears. I bring my alabaster jar. I bring my history. I kneel at the feet of the One who forgives. And I trust the words He spoke to the woman that evening as the words He speaks over me today. My sins are forgiven. My faith has saved me. I go in peace. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

My sins, which are many, are forgiven in Christ. My faith has saved me. I go in peace today. No Simon has the right to keep me from the feet of Jesus.
